titleStmt.title: Extract from the Berliner Politische Nachrichten.

head.hi: Extract from the Berliner Politische Nachrichten.

div.p: Ever since the report of a deficit of 30,000,000 marks in the Prussian budget for the coming year has been made public, attempts have been made to explain away, in a most glowing description of the financial condition of Prussia, the cause of this deficit by the myth that twenty-five millions had been appropriated to the purpose of meeting the expenses of a general increase of the wages of officials. In connection with this explanation, it was also dexterously insinuated that this appropriation was the prelude to a general increase of salaries of army officers.

The real cause, however, of the presence of so large a deficit is a very natural one. The current budget is balanced, as has been frequently explained, exclusively by the appropriation of a so-called surplus of twenty-nine millions from the year 1880–’81. For the year 1881–’82, however, a surplus to that amount is altogether out of the question. Nor are we aware that such a surplus is claimed in official sources. We can consider ourselves fortunate if our imperial stamp tax of two to three millions for the second half of the year can be appropriated to the use of the budget of 1882–’83. Furthermore, the guarantee law absorbs many more millions than was the case during the last business year. Then, too, the total income from the law courts, as shown by exhibits made last year, is less, and will be felt in the budget. These three items, which will become apparent at a glance to any unprejudiced mind on studying the question, will show that, in case all the other items are balanced, the cause of the deficit of 30,000,000 is sufficiently explained.
